pred_ddx.label: Fetal ventriculomegaly due to congenital infection

Fetal cerebral vasculopathy or thrombosi: Ultrasound and MRI findings of ventriculomegaly, irregular ventricular walls, and areas of high signal intensity on T1-weighted images and low signal intensity on T2-weighted images within the ventricles, along with a normal comprehensive workup including a TORCH panel, suggest a vascular or thrombotic etiology
Fetal ventriculomegaly due to congenital: Although the comprehensive workup, including a TORCH panel, returned within normal limits, congenital infection remains a possible cause of fetal ventriculomegaly, given the presence of bilateral ventriculomegaly and irregular ventricular walls
